title: sre-weekly-update-2026-09-26
summary: Weekly SRE update covering incidents, SLO status, on-call handoffs, key metrics, and action items for the week of 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-26.
incidents: INC-4821 (2026-09-23) - Regional autoscaler regression causing elevated tail latency and partial request throttling in us-west-2. Impact: 8% of production traffic experienced >500ms T99 for 45 minutes. Severity: P1.
INC-4815 (2026-09-21) - Degraded KV-cache hit rates after rollout of cache client v2.1.2. Impact: increased token egress and higher CPU on CPU-backed routing tier. Severity: P2.
Minor alerts - multiple transient HTTP 502 spikes in eu-central-1 during GC windows; no user-visible errors reported due to automatic retries.
incident_resolution_notes: INC-4821 root cause: a heuristic change in the autoscaler led to premature scale-down when average active sessions were calculated using a 30s window instead of 5m window. The shorter window under-sampled ramping traffic after scheduled batch jobs.
Mitigation: rolled back autoscaler agent to v3.4.1 (pre-regression) at 2026-09-23 14:12 UTC. Immediate improvement observed; T99 returned to baseline within two minutes of rollback.
Postmortem: full postmortem draft available at CONFLUENCE-Postmortem-INC-4821. Action items assigned to infra and release-engineering.
slo_status: Availability SLO (global read/write) - Target 99.95% monthly. Current burn: 0.03% for September month-to-date. After INC-4821 we used ~0.006% of budget.
Latency SLO (generation P95) - Target <200ms. Weekly average P95 is 185ms; P99 saw a spike to 620ms during INC-4821. Monitoring alert thresholds reviewed.
Error budget - Remaining for the month: ~99.88% (no escalation required).
metrics_summary: Request rate: steady at 42k QPS peak, +4% week-over-week (driven by a customer trial in APAC).
KV-cache hit rate: dropped from 87% to 63% after cache client rollout; rollback of client v2.1.2 to v2.1.0 recovered hit rate to ~86% by 2026-09-22.
Autoscaler churn: scaled events increased by 2.8x during scheduled batch windows in us-west-2 due to the regression.
oncall_handoff: Handoff 2026-09-26 08:00 UTC: Outgoing on-call: Diego Martinez. Incoming on-call: Ravi Patel.
Current pager status: No open P0s. Two P1s closed this week (INC-4821 closed by Diego).
Escalation notes: If INC-4821 regression reoccurs, page SRE lead (Maya Singh) and patch release owner (infra-release@redwood).
action_items: INFRA-1290: Add a 5m smoothed metric to autoscaler inputs and create a canary rollout job to prevent short-window regressions. Owner: Ravi Patel. Due: 2026-10-03.
PLAT-2114: Revert and redeploy cache client with improved telemetry; add unit tests for cache invalidation scenarios. Owner: Maya Singh. Due: 2026-09-30.
SRE-ops: Add a synthetic test that simulates batch-job ramps in us-west-2 during our daily chaos test. Owner: Diego Martinez. Due: 2026-10-07.
Observability: Create dashboard for autoscaler decision signals (window length, active sessions, cooldowns). Owner: observability-team. Due: 2026-10-05.
meeting_notes: Weekly SRE sync (2026-09-24): Reviewed INC-4821 timeline, validated rollback timing, confirmed postmortem owners.
Oncall retro (2026-09-25): Discussed better slack escalation flows and temporary runbooks for autoscaler regressions. Action: add autoscaler runbook subsection.
Cross-team sync with infra and release-engineering (2026-09-22): Agreed on canary policy updates and required test coverage before rolling autoscaler changes.
retrospective_notes: What went well: Fast detection via T99 alerting, quick rollback, clear owner on-call who executed runbook steps cleanly.
What to improve: Canary coverage for infra agents needs to include traffic ramp patterns; need clearer pre-rollout checklist for heuristics changes.
Follow-ups: enforce canary for infra agents with >1% traffic impact and add a mandatory post-release observability smoke test.
next_steps: Owners to update Confluence postmortem and link to this weekly update.
Implement INFRA-1290 and PLAT-2114 priorities for next two sprints.
Schedule a tabletop exercise for autoscaler regressions during Oct SRE offsite.
